result.title: Function-Space Temporal Self-Distillation for Policy Optimization
result.comment: Aryan Das, Vinay Kumar Verma: Equal Contributions. Under Review
result.summary: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) improves reasoning in language models, but scalar outcomes provide coarse supervision over response trajectories. Self-distillation offers denser token-level guidance by comparing an unassisted policy with a feedback-informed self-teacher, yet the teacher evolves with the student, creating unstable targets and motivating additional regularization. We introduce Function-Space Policy Optimization (FSPO), a single-policy framework that combines current privileged adaptation with function-space temporal consolidation. FSPO stores sparse historical next-token distributions as fixed temporal targets, providing temporal separation without maintaining a persistent teacher model. It further introduces privileged disagreement correction to explicitly suppress locally overvalued actions, reliability-adaptive grounding that strengthens reference supervision when self-generated evidence repeatedly fails, and quality and coverage-aware temporal memory that retains verified behaviors and improves privileged demonstrations. Across reasoning and tool-use benchmarks, FSPO achieves the highest average accuracy under a 5-hour training budget, improving over the strongest baseline by approximately 4% points on average while reducing peak memory from about 70 GB to 56 GB on Olmo3-7B-Instruct.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 FSPO 单策略 RLVR 框架：把稀疏的历史 next-token 分布存为固定目标做函数空间时序自蒸馏，并加入特权分歧纠正、可靠性自适应监督与质量/覆盖率感知记忆，在推理与工具使用基准上提升平均准确率并降低显存。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本 RLVR 训练方法，不涉及视觉或多模态状态；其用历史分布作固定目标以稳定自蒸馏、并按自生成证据可靠性调节监督强度的思路，可能为 LVR 中 latent 轨迹的监督与贡献分配提供训练侧线索，可供核查。
